==Airlines and destinations==

As of January 2023, the top five markets served non-stop from Birmingham are [[Atlanta]], [[Dallas/Fort Worth]], [[Charlotte, North Carolina|Charlotte]], [[Houston]], and [[Denver]]. [[American Airlines]], [[Delta Air Lines]], and [[Southwest Airlines]] serve Birmingham with mainline, narrowbody aircraft. [[Regional airline]]s provide a large share of daily air carrier service to Birmingham. The most common aircraft serving the airport are the [[Bombardier CRJ700 |Bombardier CRJ700 / CRJ900]], the [[Embraer E-Jet family|Embraer E-175]], the [[Boeing 717]], the [[Boeing 737 Next Generation|Boeing 737]] family, and the [[Airbus A319]]/[[Airbus A320 family|A320]].{{cn|date=February 2026}}

===Cargo===
In April 2023, [[Kuehne + Nagel|Kuehne+Nagel]] began twice weekly flights from [[Stuttgart Airport|Stuttgart, Germany]] to Birmingham, primarily to support the central Alabama automotive manufacturing industry.
